_meta.name: Starter template outlines
_meta.disclaimer: Template outline, not legal advice or a finished policy. Sections and questions only: no legal text is generated. Article references are checked against docs/data/laws.

templates.title: AML/CFT policy (framework)
templates.purpose: The top-level statement of how the firm manages money laundering and terrorist financing risk, and which procedures sit under it.

ask: Which legal entities, branches, products and activities does this policy cover?
Which instruments and supervisory acts does it implement?
Who must follow it: staff, agents, distributors, outsourced providers?
Who is the member of the management body responsible for compliance, and who is the compliance officer?
What are their duties, authority and reporting lines?
How do significant weaknesses in policies and controls reach the management body?
Which tasks does the firm never outsource?
Who drafts the business-wide risk assessment and who approves it?
How often is it refreshed, and which events trigger an earlier update?
How are new products, channels, technologies and customer segments assessed before launch?

sections.h: Customer due diligence and enhanced measures
ask: Which procedures set out standard and enhanced due diligence, and who owns them?
How is the customer risk profile decided and by whom?

sections.h: Ongoing monitoring and reporting of suspicions
ask: How are transactions monitored against what the firm knows about the customer?
Who approves the criteria used to detect suspicious or unusual activity?
Which procedure governs internal escalation and reporting to the FIU?

sections.h: Targeted financial sanctions and restrictive measures
ask: Which procedure covers screening, freezing and reporting?
How does the firm mitigate the risk of non-implementation and evasion of sanctions?
Which procedure sets retention periods, formats and retrieval?
Which safeguards apply to special categories of personal data processed for AML/CFT purposes?
Who must be trained, how often, and how is training documented?
How are staff assessed before taking up AML/CFT tasks, and how often is the assessment repeated?
Which internal reporting channel can staff use to report breaches?
How are reporting persons protected?

sections.h: Monitoring of compliance with this policy
ask: How is compliance with the policies and procedures monitored?
How are deficiencies identified, tracked and remediated?
Who approves this policy and who must be informed of changes?
What is the review cycle, and which events trigger an out-of-cycle review?
How do staff acknowledge each new version?

templates.title: Customer due diligence procedure
templates.purpose: Step-by-step onboarding and ongoing CDD for the teams that run it, mapped to the register's CDD obligations.

ask: Which customer types, products and channels does this procedure cover?
Which team owns each step?
Which events trigger CDD: new relationship, occasional transaction above a threshold, suspicion, doubts about earlier data, doubts about who you are dealing with?
Which thresholds apply to which of your products (see the obligation text for the amounts)?
Which minimum data set do you collect for natural persons, legal entities and persons acting on their behalf?
Which documents or electronic means do you accept to verify identity?
When is verification completed relative to establishing the relationship or carrying out the transaction?
Who checks the file before the customer is activated?
How do you identify and verify beneficial owners and ownership structures?
What do analysts do when what they find differs from the national beneficial ownership register, and who is told?

sections.h: Purpose and intended nature of the relationship
ask: Which information on purpose and expected activity is captured before onboarding?
Where is it recorded so that monitoring can compare activity against it?

sections.h: Risk classification and escalation to EDD
ask: Which factors set the customer risk tier, and who decides it?
Which results force escalation to the enhanced due diligence procedure?
Is there a second pair of eyes on high-risk approvals?
How is onboarding or the transaction stopped, and an existing relationship ended?
Who assesses whether the failure must also go to the suspicious-transaction reporting procedure?

sections.h: Ongoing due diligence and data refresh
ask: How often is each risk tier reviewed, and which events trigger an earlier review?
How are changes in customer data captured and verified?
Which CDD records are kept, where, and for how long?
Who samples files for quality and how are findings fed back?

templates.title: Enhanced due diligence and PEP procedure
templates.purpose: What changes when risk is higher or the customer is a politically exposed person.

ask: Which relationships fall under this procedure?
How does it connect to the CDD procedure?
Which higher-risk situations does the firm treat as EDD triggers?
Who confirms that a trigger applies?
Which additional information, verification and approvals are required?
How is enhanced ongoing monitoring set up and by whom?
How do you determine whether the customer, a beneficial owner or a person on whose behalf a transaction is conducted is a PEP?
Which screening sources and which frequency?

sections.h: Senior management approval and source of wealth
ask: Who gives senior management approval and what do they see?
How do you establish and verify source of wealth and source of funds?
How are family members and known close associates identified?
Which of the PEP measures apply to them in your procedure?
How long, and on what basis, do you keep treating a person as a PEP after they leave office?
Who approves lifting the status?
Where are approvals, rationale and monitoring results recorded?

templates.title: Sanctions screening procedure
templates.purpose: How the firm applies and screens against targeted financial sanctions and other restrictive measures.

ask: Which parties are screened: customers, beneficial owners, representatives, counterparties, payment parties?
Which products and flows are in scope?
Which Union and national lists do you apply, and who maintains the source of truth?
How quickly are list updates reflected in screening?
When do you screen: onboarding, periodic rescreen, every payment or transfer?
What happens to a payment while an alert is open?
Who reviews alerts, within what time, and with which evidence?
Who can close an alert, and when is a second reviewer required?
Who decides to freeze, and what is reported to which authority?
How does this connect to the suspicious-transaction reporting procedure?

sections.h: Risk of evasion and system tuning
ask: How do you assess the risk of non-implementation and evasion of sanctions?
Who tunes matching thresholds and how are changes tested and approved?
Which screening results and decisions are kept?
How is screening quality tested?

templates.title: Suspicious transaction reporting procedure
templates.purpose: How anyone at the firm escalates a suspicion and how the compliance officer assesses and reports it.

ask: Who does this procedure apply to, including agents and distributors?
How does an employee raise a suspicion, to whom, and how fast?
Does the procedure cover attempted transactions and suspicions arising when CDD cannot be completed?
Which facts and information does the compliance officer weigh, and how is the assessment documented?
How is urgency prioritised?

sections.h: Decision and reporting to the FIU
ask: Who decides to report and who transmits the report?
Which FIU and which channel and format do you use, and who keeps that current?
Who answers FIU requests for information and how is the response time tracked against the deadline in the Regulation?
When is a transaction held, who decides, and what happens if it cannot be held?

sections.h: No disclosure and protection of staff
ask: What may staff say to the customer or third parties?
How are staff who report protected from retaliation?
Where are the assessment, its rationale and any report kept, even when no report is made?
What management information goes to the compliance manager and the management body?

templates.title: Record keeping and retention policy
templates.purpose: What the firm keeps, for how long, in what form, and how it deletes and produces records.

ask: Which categories of CDD, assessment, transaction and information-sharing records are kept?
Are records kept unredacted?
For which categories do you keep references instead of copies, and how do you guarantee immediate retrieval and no alteration?
What is the retention period for each record type and when does it start?
Does national law require anything longer or shorter, and who confirmed it?
Who deletes personal data when the period ends and how is deletion evidenced?
How do you answer enquiries from the FIU or supervisors quickly and confidentially?
Who is the contact point and what is the target response time?
Which safeguards apply to special categories of data and criminal-offence data?
Who is the data protection contact for AML/CFT processing?
Who can read or change records and how is access logged?

templates.title: ICT risk and operational resilience policy (DORA)
templates.purpose: Structure for the ICT risk management framework under DORA, with the management body's responsibilities up front.

ask: Which financial-entity category does the firm fall in, and does the simplified ICT risk management framework apply?
How are proportionality criteria applied?
What does the management body approve and review, and how often?
How does it receive information on ICT third-party arrangements and major incidents?

sections.h: ICT risk management framework and control function
ask: Who is responsible for managing and overseeing ICT risk and how is independence ensured?
How often is the framework reviewed, and which events trigger an earlier review?

sections.h: Identification of functions, assets and risks
ask: Where are ICT-supported business functions and assets documented and classified?
How often is classification and the risk scenario set reviewed?
Which security policies, tools and monitoring are in place?
How are detection mechanisms and alert thresholds defined and tested?
Which critical or important functions does the ICT business continuity policy protect?
What are the backup scope and frequency, and how are restoration procedures tested?
How are ICT-related incidents detected, recorded, classified and escalated?
Who decides that an incident is major and who notifies the competent authority?
What does the testing programme include, how often does each test run, and who tracks findings to closure?
How are post-incident reviews run and fed back into the framework?
How is ICT security awareness and training delivered?
Which policy governs ICT third-party providers?

templates.title: Outsourcing and third-party risk policy
templates.purpose: How the firm decides what to outsource, contracts for it, monitors providers and exits, including AML/CFT limits.

ask: Which arrangements are in scope: ICT services, AML/CFT tasks, agents, other operational functions?
Who classifies an arrangement as supporting a critical or important function?
Who owns the register of contractual arrangements and how often is it updated?
How is the register reported to the management body and to the competent authority on request?
Which checks run before signing: suitability, risks, concentration, conflicts of interest, information security standards?
Who approves the decision to contract?
Which clauses are mandatory in every contract, and which additional ones apply to critical or important functions?
Who reviews contracts against the checklist?

sections.h: AML/CFT tasks that can and cannot be outsourced
ask: Which AML/CFT tasks are outsourced, and was the supervisor notified before they started?
How does the firm confirm that approval of policies, decisions on risk profile and onboarding, and reporting to the FIU stay in-house, subject to the exceptions in the Regulation?
If the firm uses agents or, as a crypto-asset service provider, outsources operational functions, which additional conditions apply?
How often is each provider reviewed and audited, and who does it?
Under which circumstances can the contract be terminated, and what is the exit plan?

templates.title: AML/CFT training and awareness standard
templates.purpose: Who is trained on what, how often, how it is evidenced, and how staff confirm they have read the policies.

ask: Which employees, agents and distributors must be trained, and why?
How do you know the list is complete?
What does each role need to be able to recognise and do?
How is content tied to the firm's own risks and procedures?

sections.h: Frequency and onboarding of new staff
ask: How soon after joining, and how often afterwards, must training be completed?
Where are attendance, results and content versions recorded?
How are skills, knowledge, good repute and integrity assessed for staff who take part in AML/CFT compliance, and how often is it repeated?
How do staff confirm they have read each new policy version, and what happens when they do not?
